```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5)
library(SpatialMethodsWorkbench)
```

This vignette exercises the spatial and network analysis family with 72 synthetic observations. The small permutation count and compact data are intended for reproducibility checks, not final analysis settings.

```{r data}
d <- demo_spatial_data(n = 72, seed = 2026)
features <- c("epithelial", "APC", "CTL", "Treg", "T_helper")
mapping <- list(
  x = "x", y = "y", z = NULL, zone = "zone", id = "sample_id",
  outcome = "disease", exposure = "epithelial", mediator = "APC"
)
```

## Spatial exploration and autocorrelation

```{r spatial-qc}
spatial_qc <- run_analysis(
  "spatial_qc", d, mapping, features,
  list(feature = "epithelial", neighbors = 6, permutations = 19, seed = 2026)
)
spatial_qc$table
```

```{r spatial-qc-plot}
spatial_qc$plot
```

The output reports the configured neighbor graph, statistic, permutation calculation, and provenance. It does not establish a biological mechanism.

## Region-aware conditional network

```{r conditional-network}
conditional <- run_analysis(
  "conditional_network", d, mapping, features,
  list(threshold = 0.15, ridge = 0.05, by_zone = TRUE)
)
head(conditional$table, 10)
conditional$summary
```

```{r conditional-network-plot}
conditional$plot
```

The stored matrices can be audited directly.

```{r matrix-names}
names(conditional$matrices)
vapply(conditional$matrices, nrow, integer(1))
```

Edges are regularized conditional-association summaries. The vignette intentionally stops at reproducible output inspection.

## Public advanced engines

The following calls use the same 72-row table. They are not evaluated while building the vignette because runtime depends on the installed public engines and local hardware.

### ISPat 2D

The ISPat 2D path calls `ISPAT3D::ispat3d_fit_2d()` from the CRAN package ISPAT3D (0.3.1 or newer): a Matérn-3/2 Vecchia GP is fitted per marker within each zone-section group, and a shared-plus-zone factor covariance is fitted by Gaussian maximum likelihood. The small anchor and iteration settings below are software smoke values; the package defaults (rank 5, up to 5,000 anchors, 15 neighbors, 30 GP iterations) are the analysis settings. Because `sample_id` is unique per row it is not treated as a section label, and the result notes say so.

```{r ispat, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("ISPAT3D")

ispat <- run_analysis(
  "ispat", d, mapping, features,
  list(
    rank = 2L, anchor_min = 12L, anchor_max = 24L, gp_neighbors = 5L,
    gp_maxit = 3L, factor_maxit = 60L, threads = 1L, seed = 2026L,
    threshold = 0.05
  )
)
ispat$summary
names(ispat$matrices)      # one signed partial-correlation matrix per zone
head(ispat$table)
table(ispat$gp_log$status)
ispat$notes
ispat$plot
```

### GP-GHS

The short chain below is a software smoke check. Increase Monte Carlo settings and perform convergence assessment for research use. GPGHS 1.0 selects a predictor when its group shrinkage factor falls below `edge_threshold` (0.5 in the article) and combines the two directed decisions with the AND rule.

```{r gpghs, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("sagnikbhadury/GP-GHS")

gpghs <- run_analysis(
  "gpghs", d, mapping, features,
  list(
    basis = 3L, nu = 1.5, nmc = 200L, burn = 50L, thin = 2L,
    edge_threshold = 0.5, symmetry = "AND", min_detect = 0, cores = 1L, seed = 1L
  )
)
gpghs$summary
head(gpghs$table)          # GPGHS score, sign, sign change, and RMS weight per selected edge
gpghs$plot
```

The GP-GHS graph uses the fitted symmetric adjacency for topology and the smaller directional RMS of the posterior mean coefficient fields for edge width. It does not use kappa as a visual weight, and it does not assign a single sign to a field that can change sign across space; the edge table carries the GPGHS sign label instead.

Use `method_citations("ispat")` and `method_citations("gpghs")` to retrieve the required software and method references.
